## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 77 (*Cīvaradāna-sikkhamānana-vuṭṭhāpana*) is an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) in the Vinaya Piṭaka concerning the ordination of female probationers (*sikkhamānā*) [SuttaCentral]. In the origin narrative, the nun Thullanandā promises to ordain (*vuṭṭhāpana*) a trainee nun on the condition that the trainee present her with a robe; after receiving the robe-cloth, however, Thullanandā neither ordains her nor makes any effort to have her ordained [SuttaCentral; Sujato 2009]. Ute Hüsken observes that this rule does not merely condemn the receipt of a gift as bribery, but penalizes a nun's failure to fulfill a conditional commitment to ordain someone when no obstacles prevent it [Hüsken 1997]. Bhikkhu Sujato also analyzes this passage to illustrate Vinaya usage, contrasting the request for *upasampadā* with the verb *vuṭṭhāpana* ("to raise up" or ordain) [Sujato 2009]. An English translation is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

SuttaCentral records corresponding parallels in the Pali *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (pc 77) and the *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* (pc 77), as well as in the Bhikṣuṇī Vibhaṅgas and Prātimokṣas of the Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Sarvāstivāda, and Tibetan Mūlasarvāstivāda traditions [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus detects significant Pali-internal text reuse with related Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga rules—most notably with Pācittiya 78 (Bi-Vb Pc 78, sharing over 6,500 characters, §0.1–2.2.8 ↔ §0.1–2.25) and Pācittiya 34—as well as the *Parivāra* (Pvr 2.1, 2.2) and subcommentarial texts [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language automated alignments, DharmaNexus also identifies passages matching the Sanskrit *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* [DharmaNexus].
